'''Reinhard Diestel''' (born 1959){{r|dnb}} is a German mathematician specializing in [[graph theory]], including the interplay among [[graph minor]]s, [[matroid theory]], [[tree decomposition]], and infinite graphs. He holds the chair of discrete mathematics at the [[University of Hamburg]].{{r|uhdm}}

==Education and career==
Diestel has a Ph.D. from the [[University of Cambridge]] in England, completed in 1986.{{r|cv}} His dissertation, ''Simplicial Decompositions and Universal Graphs'', was supervised by [[Béla Bollobás]].{{r|mg}}

He continued at Cambridge as a fellow of [[St. John's College, Cambridge]] until 1990. In 1994, he took a professorship at the [[Chemnitz University of Technology]], and in 1999 he was given his current chair at the University of Hamburg.{{r|cv}}

At Hamburg, his doctoral students have included [[Daniela Kühn]] and [[Maya Stein]].{{r|mg}}

==Books==
Diestel's books include:
*''Graph Decompositions: A Study in Infinite Graph Theory'' (Oxford University Press, 1990){{r|gd}}
*''Graph Theory'' ([[Graduate Texts in Mathematics]] 173, Springer, 1997; 6th ed., 2024). Originally published in German as ''Graphentheorie'' (1996), and translated into Chinese, Japanese, and Russian.{{r|gt}}
*''Tangles: A Structural Approach to Artificial Intelligence in the Empirical Sciences'' (Cambridge University Press, 2024; {{arxiv|2006.01830}})
